answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a per-agent stake bonded on-chain: each identity must lock a minimum deposit and wait a cooling period before attesting. A fake account needs its own deposit, and slashing burns it when coordinated votes contradict peers. To farm rewards an attacker must finance a whole grove of deposits, tie it up across every cooling window, and risk total loss on a detected ring. Because recycling is delayed, each extra identity still costs real capital and the attack horizon widens, since funds cannot be cardstacked into new seats. A saffron-tier flag triggers review.
